If the coordinator would rather have the worker's exact bytes back, `git checkout -- explorations/compile-ladder/ladder.tsv explorations/compile-ladder/summary.txt` restores the committed versions; re-running `python3 explorations/compile-ladder/classify.py` reproduces mine in seconds.

Untouched: `explorations/coordinator/FACTS.md`, `explorations/fortress-gap-ledger.md` (rows 302 and 303 are unchanged, at lines 389 and 390), `explorations/microgpt-run-c-handover.md`, and both runtime files.

## Preparation done, so a follow-up worker does not repeat it

I read PLAN.md, the RULES block of `ladder-workflow.js`, FACTS.md's execution-model section, and both perf-probe reports, and settled the two edits and the timing recipe:

- **Ledger 302**, `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/runtimeSystem/BaseTask.java:248`. The edit is one line: wrap `debug("inATransaction: ftr = " + ftr + " task = " + ftr.getTask());` in `if (debug)`. `debug` is `private static Boolean debug = false;` at line 50 and the `debug(String)` method at 52-53 already tests it, so the flag is simply consulted too late. Worth noting for whoever does it: the same eager-concatenation pattern sits at lines 183, 186, 193, 195, 207, 234, 242 and 258 of the same file. Only 248 is on the hot path and only 248 is in scope, but 234 (`getCurrentTransaction`) is called immediately after 248 whenever a transaction is live and is the obvious second candidate if one edit does not move the number enough.
- **Ledger 303**, `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/runtimeValues/FFloatLiteral.java`. Confirmed: `private String val;` with `FFloatLiteral(double val) { this(new Double(val).toString()); }` and `asRR64() { return FRR64.make(Double.valueOf(val)); }` — so the generated loop pays a `double`→decimal format *and* a decimal→`double` parse per literal per iteration. The smallest fix is a cached `double dval` field: the `String` constructor sets `dval = Double.valueOf(val)`, the `double` constructor sets `dval = val` and leaves `val` null, `toString()` falls back to `Double.toString(dval)`, `asRR64()` returns `FRR64.make(dval)`. One wrinkle to decide rather than stumble over: `asRR32()` is `FRR32.make(Float.valueOf(val))`, so on the double-constructed path it would become `(float) dval`; that is a narrowing instead of a re-parse of the shortest round-trip decimal, which differs only in double-rounding corner cases but is a real behaviour change and belongs in the report's "Not verified" section. This is the compiler-side class; the interpreter has its own unrelated `interpreter/evaluator/values/FFloatLiteral.java`.
- **Found while reading, not in either probe report and worth the coordinator's attention**: `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/asmbytecodeoptimizer/RemoveLiteralCoercions.java` already implements exactly the constant-folding the boxing report proposes — `removeFloatLiterals` and `removeFloatLiterals2` rewrite the `FFloatLiteral.make(D)` + `coerce_RR64` pair to a single `FRR64.make(D)`. Its only caller is `ByteCodeOptimizer.java:137`, which is not on the normal `fortress compile` path, so the optimizer is dormant. That directory is outside my boundary, so I did nothing with it, but it means the team had already written the fix and it is unreached — relevant to how rung 0 is framed and possibly a cheaper route than editing the runtime class.
- **Timing recipe**: `explorations/perf-probes/boxing/run-all.sh` times `fortress run bench1t` three times and takes the median of the `loop_ns` the program prints itself. `bench1t` exercises both defects at once (two float literals inside the loop, a `:=` accumulator); `explorations/perf-probes/kernels/bench1h.fss` isolates the transaction check alone with the literals hoisted, and is the one the JFR profile attributed 88.9% to, so timing both separates the two fixes. Baseline medians to beat: bench1t 9.3441 s, bench1h 6.0732 s.
- **Cache state**: the ladder ran against a private cache tree (`FORTRESS_CACHES` under the scratchpad), so `default_repository/caches/` is untouched. `bytecode_cache/` already holds `fortress.AnyType.jar`, `fortress.CompilerBuiltin.jar`, `fortress.CompilerLibrary.jar`, `CompilerAlgebra.jar` and `CompilerSystem.jar` from 2026-09-16, so the 100-120 s library-order rebuild is not needed — only `fortress compile bench1t` (and `bench1h`) in the probe directories.

`df -h /` reports 4.0 GB available, 90% used — above the 500 MB floor but not comfortable. The ladder's own log ends at 4184488 KB free and nothing has consumed since. `/tmp/fortress*rats` and `ProjectFortress/test-tmp` were clean at every check; `experiment/env.sh` sweeps the former when sourced.

## What the coordinator needs to decide

The baseline worker appears to have died before writing its prose report. The machine is idle and the tree is clean of source edits, so either can start immediately.

No permission was denied at any point.

- **Ledger 302**, `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/runtimeSystem/BaseTask.java:248`. The edit is one line: wrap `debug("inATransaction: ftr = " + ftr + " task = " + ftr.getTask());` in `if (debug)`. `debug` is `private static Boolean debug = false;` at line 50 and the `debug(String)` method at 52-53 already tests it, so the flag is simply consulted too late. Worth noting for whoever does it: the same eager-concatenation pattern sits at lines 183, 186, 193, 195, 207, 234, 242 and 258 of the same file. Only 248 is on the hot path and only 248 is in scope, but 234 (`getCurrentTransaction`) is called immediately after 248 whenever a transaction is live and is the obvious second candidate if one edit does not move the number enough.
- **Ledger 303**, `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/runtimeValues/FFloatLiteral.java`. Confirmed: `private String val;` with `FFloatLiteral(double val) { this(new Double(val).toString()); }` and `asRR64() { return FRR64.make(Double.valueOf(val)); }` — so the generated loop pays a `double`→decimal format *and* a decimal→`double` parse per literal per iteration. The smallest fix is a cached `double dval` field: the `String` constructor sets `dval = Double.valueOf(val)`, the `double` constructor sets `dval = val` and leaves `val` null, `toString()` falls back to `Double.toString(dval)`, `asRR64()` returns `FRR64.make(dval)`. One wrinkle to decide rather than stumble over: `asRR32()` is `FRR32.make(Float.valueOf(val))`, so on the double-constructed path it would become `(float) dval`; that is a narrowing instead of a re-parse of the shortest round-trip decimal, which differs only in double-rounding corner cases but is a real behaviour change and belongs in the report's "Not verified" section. This is the compiler-side class; the interpreter has its own unrelated `interpreter/evaluator/values/FFloatLiteral.java`.

That directory is outside my boundary, so I did nothing with it, but it means the team had already written the fix and it is unreached — relevant to how rung 0 is framed and possibly a cheaper route than editing the runtime class.
